The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) technical indicator shows the relationship between two exponential moving averages, the MACD line and signal line. The MACD line is the difference between a 12-day EMA and a 26-day EMA, while the signal line is a 9-day EMA of the MACD line. If the MACD line crosses above the signal line, this is considered a bullish sign. If the MACD line crosses below the signal line, this is considered a bearish sign. This technical indicator is often used to identify trend reversals and divergences. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) technical indicator measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate whether a stock is overbought or over sold. A reading above 70 indicates that the stock is overbought and a reading below 30 indicates the stock is over sold. Fibonacci Retracement is a technical analysis technique that identifies areas that are likely to act as support or resistance as the price of an asset moves. The Fibonacci retracement levels are calculated by taking the difference between the high and low prices of a recent swing and multiplying it by the Fibonacci ratios. Bollinger Bands are a technical analysis indicator that provides the volatility of the price and potential areas of support and resistance. The upper Bollinger Band is a moving average plus two standard deviations, while the lower Bollinger Band is a moving average minus two standard deviations.
